hypotheses.confidence_note: Conditional two-second local prototype, not a calibrated reconstruction or verified trajectory. Initial ego speed is 6.0906 m/s; 4 m/s is a deceleration preference, not an assumed initial state. Revision 1 repairs the truck and taxi premise scopes: each now explicitly covers both its actual pre-reference alignment interval and its separately stated conditional future modes through two seconds. No geometry, obstacle, residual or safety limit has been removed or relaxed. Road edges and actor poses remain approximate visual hypotheses. More distant parked rows, rear vehicles outside the domain, hidden pedestrians, departures exceeding the declared bounds and new entrants are excluded only under prototype_local_scope. No optimization, independent dynamics/collision verification or simulated prefix has been executed here.

premises.statement: Model only this finite local domain for two seconds, using the convex paved route patch separately specified as road. Assume no new unobserved entrant, pedestrian, opening door or object enters this domain or the route from occlusions during the horizon. Observed more distant parking rows and rear vehicles outside the domain remain parked and do not enter it. This excludes world conditions rather than claiming they are absent. The nearby truck, taxi, silver SUV and white hatchback are explicitly retained. Road geometry follows visible curb/pavement transitions, with approximate near-edge continuation around the current footprint; grass islands and parking bays are not driving space. The intended short route remains on the local approach before the main left bend.

Adopt approximate rigid body-size priors: light flatbed truck 5.5 by 2.0 m, taxi 4.6 by 1.8 m, silver SUV 4.5 by 1.85 m, white hatchback 4.4 by 1.75 m. Use visible body extents, calibrated viewing axes and perspective to estimate ground-XY positions and curb separation. These fixed dimension hypotheses apply at the cited acquisitions, their alignment intervals and the future horizon. Local pavement is approximately continuous with modest grade; no certified flat-ground reconstruction is asserted. Pose, scale and boundary errors are represented by declared finite noncalibrated residual hypotheses.

The vehicles appear aligned in parking bays rather than moving along the aisle. Adopt stationary reference poses for two seconds. Reasonable adverse variants permit total center displacement from each reference pose up to 0.2 m in any direction and yaw departure up to 0.03 rad at any time, without a larger pull-out. Expanded adverse rectangles enclose the complete bodies for all these poses throughout the closed interval, including the native body at zero. This stationary-or-small-motion inventory is complete only within these explicit conditions.

This is a joint acquisition-alignment and conditional parked-continuation premise, justified by the truck's visible parking-bay placement in the front-left capture. During [-0.008,0], including the actual acquisition at -0.007616 s, assume ground speed at most 0.2 m/s and negligible yaw change; evidence-to-reference displacement is bounded by 0.002 m under both retained scenarios. The native evidence position is estimated in fixed reference axes using supplied ego pose, with additional alignment residual 0.25 m; ego compensation alone does not establish stationarity. Separately during [0,2], truck_stationary holds the native reference pose, while truck_small_motion permits center displacement up to 0.2 m in any direction and yaw departure up to 0.03 rad throughout the interval, as in parked_future. The 0.002 m bound applies only to acquisition-to-reference alignment, not to future displacement. A larger departure is excluded conditionally, not ruled out by observation.

anchors.rationale: The individually visible white hatchback has a nearly side-on body in the reference front image. A 4.4 m compact-hatchback length is an explicit class-size prior matching its native body geometry, not a measured dimension.
The individually visible cab-and-flatbed truck in the cited front-left image supports a light-truck length prior of 5.5 m, matching its native body hypothesis.

metric_scale_support.metric_reasoning: The white hatchback spans roughly 330 image pixels in a predominantly transverse pose. With front focal length about 1266 pixels and the 4.4 m length prior, its body-center range is approximately 16–18 m, with lateral offset about 7 m right. The nearer partially clipped silver SUV is assigned approximately 10.5 m forward and 7 m right. Truck and taxi ranges use their body-size priors and respective calibrated side-camera viewing directions, transformed with supplied ego acquisition poses. Visible aisle curbs imply approximately 7–9 m pavement width locally, narrowing toward the bend. The convex road polygon follows this local straight portion and includes the current 4.6 by 1.8 m ego footprint; 0.4 m boundary uncertainty is retained. These are falsifiable model estimates rather than calibration-certified depths.
